title: A smooth morphism is etale on an affine open where the differentials vanish
statement: Let $g:U\to S$ be a smooth morphism of schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $V\subseteq S$ and $W\subseteq U$ be affine open subschemes [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with $g(W)\subseteq V$, let $R=\mathcal O_S(V)$, $A=\mathcal O_U(W)$ and $R\to A$ the ring map corresponding to $g|_W:W\to V$, and assume that the module of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{A/R}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] is zero. Then the restriction $g|_W:W\to S$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: Morphisms, Section 02GH: the sentence before Definition 02GI (line 8050: 'a ring map R -> A is said to be etale if it is smooth and Omega_{A/R} = 0', Algebra Definition 00U1), Definition 02GI (definition-etale, line 8058), Lemma 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize: R -> A is smooth for affine opens of a smooth morphism), Lemmas 02GP (open immersion etale) and 02GN (composition); equivalently Lemma 01VF (lemma-smooth-flat), Lemma 02G5 (lemma-unramified-omega-zero) and Lemma 02GE for the clauses of [def-weil-etale-morphism]; smoothness of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] is Definition 01V5 by more-morphisms.tex Lemma 02H6

proof.text: (The restriction $W\to V$ is smooth.) Let $j_W:W\to U$ and $j_V:V\to S$ be the inclusions of the open subschemes. Since $g(W)\subseteq V$, by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] there is a unique morphism $g_{W,V}:W\to V$ with $j_V\circ g_{W,V}=g\circ j_W=g|_W$; this is the morphism $g|_W:W\to V$ of the statement. Since $g$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], $g_{W,V}$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](a).

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize, line 7048), last sentence: if f is smooth, then for open subschemes U of X, V of S with f(U) in V the restriction U -> V is smooth

proof.text: ($g_{W,V}$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the ring map $\varphi:R\to A$.) Let $\varphi:R=\mathcal O_S(V)\to A=\mathcal O_U(W)$ be the ring map induced by $g$ ($g^\sharp_V$ followed by restriction from $g^{-1}(V)$ to $W$), which is the ring map of the statement, and let $\iota_W:\operatorname{Spec}A\to U$, $\iota_V:\operatorname{Spec}R\to S$ be the canonical open immersions with images $W$ and $V$ of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points] [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; by their construction there, $\iota_W=j_W\circ\alpha$ and $\iota_V=j_V\circ\beta$ for the isomorphisms $\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}A\to W$, $\beta:\operatorname{Spec}R\to V$ inverse to $W\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$, $V\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-induced-ring-map-spec-square] applied to $g$, $W$, $V$: $\iota_V\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi=g\circ\iota_W$. Hence $j_V\circ(\beta\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi)=\iota_V\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi=g\circ j_W\circ\alpha=j_V\circ(g_{W,V}\circ\alpha)$. The two morphisms $\beta\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ and $g_{W,V}\circ\alpha$ from $\operatorname{Spec}A$ to $V$ have the same composite with $j_V$, so by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] (applied to this composite, whose image lies in $V$) they are equal: $\beta\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi=g_{W,V}\circ\alpha$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine, line 841: morphisms into an affine scheme are determined by the ring map on global sections); the identification of f|_U : U -> V with Spec of the induced ring map O_S(V) -> O_X(U) is used without comment in Morphisms Lemma 01V6 and Definition 02GI

proof.text: ($\varphi$ is a smooth ring map.) In [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](c) take $f=g_{W,V}:W\to V$, $f'=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi:\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and the isomorphisms $u=\alpha$, $v=\beta$; step 2 gives $v\circ f'=f\circ u$, and $f$ is smooth by step 1, so $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], $\varphi$ is a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]: $A$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra, $H_1(L_{A/R})=0$, and $\Omega_{A/R}$ is finite projective.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize), (1) implies (2): for affine opens U of X, V of S with f(U) in V the ring map O_S(V) -> O_X(U) is smooth; smoothness of def-sbc-smooth-morphisms agrees with Definition 01V5 by more-morphisms.tex Lemma 02H6

proof.text: ($\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ is etale.) By step 3, $A$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra and $H_1(L_{A/R})=0$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], and $\Omega_{A/R}=0$ by hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. So $\varphi$ is an etale ring map in the sense of Algebra, Definition 00U1 as stated in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine], and by that lemma $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi:\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: Morphisms, Section 02GH, sentence before Definition 02GI (line 8050: a ring map R -> A is etale if it is smooth and Omega_{A/R} = 0, Algebra Definition 00U1), and Definition 02GI (definition-etale, line 8058)

proof.text: ($g|_W:W\to S$ is etale.) An isomorphism of schemes is a homeomorphism onto the whole target, which is open, and induces an isomorphism of structure sheaves, so it is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]; hence $\alpha^{-1}$ and $\beta$ are open immersions, and so is $j_V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1) $\alpha^{-1}$, $\beta$ and $j_V$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. By step 2, $g_{W,V}=\beta\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi\circ\alpha^{-1}$, which is etale by step 4 and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](2) (applied twice). Finally $g|_W=g\circ j_W=j_V\circ g_{W,V}$ (step 1) is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](2).

proof_origin.place: Morphisms, Section 02GH (Definition 02GI with the definition of an etale ring map recalled at line 8050), Lemma 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize), Lemmas 02GP and 02GN; Schemes Lemma 01I1 for the identification of g|_W with Spec of R -> A. Stacks does not state the lemma as such: with Definition 02GI it is immediate; the steps make the identifications explicit for the DAG's definitions
